column1: # Differences between the routes of the formal proofs and the paper's proofs, each with its reason.
# Format: label<TAB>±other<TAB>reason. See Section 7 of REPORT.md. The routes of the papers are in docs/paper_routes.tsv.
# A row with the label `*` records a result used without citation throughout. Each paper has a section below.
# Basic facts about the objects, used without citation throughout.

column3: That two blobs with an arc in common are equal (line 139) is what makes "the blob of a site" meaningful. The paper uses it without citing it wherever it speaks of a blob; here `IsFullyDecomposedFor.breaksAt_unique`, `exists_optimal_piece` and `Decomp.exists_inflate_net` use it.
`G_S(M) = G(M + S)` (lines 152, 160) is the definition of the rooted graph as far as the paper is concerned, and it passes between the two without citation.
The paper contracts blobs, so it needs them well defined. `Network.blobbedTree` is the quotient by the arcs on cycles, with no mention of blobs, so `blobbedTree_isTree` doesn't use the fact.

`IsDominantFor` is the dominance for all pairs of sites, so uniqueness needs only that one pair has one dominant pair of states (`IsDominantPair.eq`). The existence of a dominant pair (line 200) isn't needed; `exists_isDominantFor` uses it.
`IsDominantFor` is the dominance for all pairs of sites, which is what Lemma 1 gives in `exists_isDominantFor`. Uniqueness is then a statement about one pair, and doesn't use Lemma 1.

The paper's "every row has value 1 in exactly one column of `B(C)`" is used only for "at most one": `charValue_disjoint` proves that from the definition, without the existence half that `existsUnique_charValue_eq_true` adds.
The Lean statement takes `IsTBar` as a hypothesis, where the paper takes the tree it has just built. `exists_isTBar` is what gives the tree, and `exists_network_of_pieces` applies both.

Line 299 uses without stating it that each edge at `v_C` carries a character of `C` ("the edge incident with `v_C` that is labeled by character `c`"), which line 277 declines to assert. It is true, and `IsTBar.exists_side_true`, behind the frame of the network, needs it (`adj_center_labelled`).

Departure, recorded in the docstring of `theorem10`: line 560's equality is false for identical columns (`g:visible_false`). `exists_row_of_eq_haplotypeBound` (`g:thm10_pair`) has the same count on one site per distinct column, and gives the pair of labels on two sites. `sMinDecomposable_of_haplotype_tight` (`g:thm10_distinct`) is the paper's proof, for distinct columns.

The same departure: Corollary 2 asks for every node visible. `theorem10` has what the proof of Corollary 2 uses from that, that no recombination node breaks two components (`breaksAt_unique_of_eq_haplotypeBound`), and applies Theorem 7 as that proof does (`sMinDecomposable_of_isOptimalRooted`).
Line 559 only shows that a network with `H(M + S)` nodes is optimal. The hypothesis `H(M + S) = R_S(M)` gives an optimal network with that many nodes directly, so the inequality isn't needed.
The step that replaces visibility: see `-ext:haplotype_equality`.

`Derives` has the rows exactly at the leaves, and the proof applies Theorem 10 to a network in which a row can be at an internal node: `exists_derives_of_displays` trims it. The paper's "phylogenetic network for `M`" allows this directly.
Proposition 6 is Lemma 7 at the last index, and the Lean proofs of both are the same two helpers, `rStarVec_feasible` and `sum_rStarVec_le`, so `proposition6` doesn't call `lemma7`.
`corollary8` is stated for the sum of `rStarVec`, the minimum of Lemma 7, and takes its feasibility from `rStarVec_feasible`, the helper behind `lemma7`, not from the statement of `lemma7`.
`Derives` has the rows exactly at the leaves, so the network with the site put back is trimmed (`exists_derives_of_displays`). The source's sample histories have no such condition.

Departure, recorded in the head of `SampleHistory.lean`: the source passes to the reduced data by Proposition 2, and Lean argues on a history, a set of nodes of a network closed under parents. Only the inequality `R_{S'} ≤ R_S` is used, in the form that a network with the rows on some sites has them on fewer.

`Rh_le_Rs` compares the two bounds by the monotonicity of Algorithm 1 in the local bounds, `algorithm1_mono`, which comes from its optimality. The source says only "for any given data set `R_s ≥ R_h ≥ R_m`".
`hudsonKaplan_isOptimalValue` is `isOptimalValue_countUpTo` at the last site, which has the same statement for the region up to any site, and the step that the source leaves out (`exists_pierce`).
